articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 5: Chiefs are all the way back at 4-0, though injury concerns linger
articles.summary: The Chiefs went 6-11 last season, which looks like an aberration.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

Bad news for all those who thought the Kansas City Chiefs' dynasty was over.

The Chiefs might be an anomaly. No other NFL dynasty had a bad season in the middle of it. The Patriots missed the playoffs in 2008 a season after going 16-0, but they were 11-5 and missed on a tiebreaker. The 1982 49ers were 3-6, but that was a weird strike season. When any other NFL dynasty had a terrible season, the run was over at that point.

They're 4-0 after beating a Raiders team that was off to a 3-0 start. While there was plenty of faith in the Chiefs bouncing back this season, there were reasons to wonder as well. Kansas City went 6-11 last season, and that included 6-8 in Patrick Mahomes' starts. Mahomes tore his ACL on Dec. 14 and there was concern he wouldn't be available for the start of the season nine months later.

There were questions on the roster, not just the recurring issues at receiver but also losing three valuable starters from the secondary in free agency and a trade. Those questions have subsided. Mahomes looks healthy and pretty good. The excellence of free-agent addition Kenneth Walker at running back has given the Chiefs a dimension they haven't had in a long time. Kansas City is third in DVOA. It's fourth in EPA (expected points added per play) on offense and ninth in EPA allowed on defense; Chicago and Jacksonville are the only other teams ranked top nine in both.

Yet, there's concern. KC's receivers are now dealing with injuries. Tyquan Thornton, who was playing a big role because Xavier Worthy has done almost nothing in his third season, is out for months with a gruesome ankle injury . Rashee Rice suffered a hamstring injury on Sunday. The line has been without left tackle Josh Simmons all season due to injury. Walker is great but he has never had a huge workload in the NFL and will be asked to carry even more of the offense going forward. If Walker fades or gets injured, it could get scary.

But every team has concerns. For the Chiefs, all that matters is they are undefeated and with very promising balance through four weeks. There was a question after last season's stunning fall if the Chiefs' dynasty was over. The Chiefs have seemingly provided the answer to that.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 4 of the NFL season:

The Dolphins battled at Minnesota, and if they didn't get unlucky on Chris Bell barely stepping out of bounds before catching a long touchdown and getting an illegal touching penalty, maybe they'd have a win. But it's another loss, and Miami's offense is still hard to watch. Unfortunately for Dolphins fans, it's a familiar feeling.

The problem might be that the Dolphins can't really get an evaluation of Malik Willis. He has not played well. He had 85 yards passing and was inaccurate on several throws. But given the junior varsity roster around him, is he getting a fair look? The Dolphins need to figure it out before the 2027 NFL Draft, though it seems inevitable they'll be taking a quarterback.

Maybe it was just a half of garbage time with the Ravens trying to just run out the clock without Lamar Jackson after halftime, but there were some signs of progress from the Titans.

They outscored Baltimore 11-0 in the second half. Cam Ward finished 20-of-31 passing for 222 yards and a touchdown. Carnell Tate might have been the biggest story for Tennessee, as the fourth overall pick of the draft had nine catches for 145 yards. In the first three weeks combined he had 13 catches for 123 yards. There were still issues. Tate fumbled twice, losing one. Ward threw an interception on a flip pass that went off Tony Pollard's hands and Tennessee had just one scoring drive in the first half as Baltimore pulled away. Tennessee gave up 24 points in the first half. But at least it was a little better in the second half.

"We have to really hone in on the bad plays, and how we can limit that," Ward said, via the team's site . "We have to limit the bad plays on both sides of the ball, not just offense."

At some point, Buccaneers ownership will ask how the team put itself in a position that it had to start undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at quarterback with its season slipping away. Daniels was the first undrafted rookie QB to start a game in Week 4 or earlier since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. Daniels did the best he could in a tough situation, completing 19-of-27 passing for 148 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions with 55 yards rushing. But the Buccaneers came up short, scoring only 14 points.

Head coach Todd Bowles is firmly on the hot seat . General manager Jason Licht did a great job constructing the 2020 Bucs team that won a title, but Tampa Bay's record is 93-108 in his 13 seasons as GM. If this season continues to get worse with Daniels starting, or even with Baker Mayfield rushing back from a thumb injury, nobody should feel too safe.

Maybe the second half, when the Chargers outscored Seattle 17-10, is a sign that things are turning around. Probably not though. Seattle led 20-6 at halftime. Herbert was 5 of 14 for 36 passing yards and two interceptions with a passer rating of 4.8 at halftime. Seattle let its guard down in the second half and allowed LA to have a shot at tying the game in the final two minutes. With the game on the line, the Seahawks sacked Herbert, causing a fumble the Chargers lost. That seemed more like the 2026 Chargers.

The Chargers lost their last three games last season, including one in the playoffs. The seven-game losing streak is the longest of Jim Harbaugh's entire coaching career in college or the pros, according to NFL Media researcher John Todd . Harbaugh should turn things around. But it's possible the Chargers are buried by the time that happens.

We might be seeing the Jets start to unravel. They've lost three in a row since beating the Titans in Week 1, and Sunday's performance was miserable for them. They ran just 32 plays compared to 89 for the Bears, a massive discrepancy. The last time there was a gap that large was when the 1999 Browns, an expansion team, ran 28 plays to 90 for the Steelers ( h/t FootballPerspective.com ).

Late in the third quarter, Geno Smith was 5-for-11 passing for 44 yards. The Jets had some offensive injuries but the Bears were using their backup quarterback, so it's not a great excuse.

The Jets' offense has looked much better than that this season so perhaps it was just a truly horrible afternoon. But at 1-3, the season could get away from New York quickly.

Jeremiyah Love's comments after the fourth game of his rookie season were odd. Love played 30 snaps, six fewer than Tyler Allgeier, and the Cardinals lost a game that was up in the air until the final play. It was weird usage. Love said he was being managed and he was good with it. He said he would "probably just hinder the team" playing more and he said he told the coaches, "I think Tyler or Bam [Knight] can exert themselves a little bit more," according to ESPN's Josh Weinfuss . Love said the high-ankle sprain he had in preseason isn't an issue anymore, just general wear and tear and management by coaches.

"It's been a long year for me," Love said, via Weinfuss. "Body sometimes is down, body sometimes is tired. So it's just managing those things. Coaches know that this is probably going to be the longest year of my life. And just want to manage that workload."

Love tweaked his other ankle in Sunday's loss , head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday, raising the need to manage the rookie's workdload.

Love was the third overall pick of the NFL Draft and has looked good (4.1 yards per carry) even though his snaps have been limited. The Cardinals shouldn't be running the third pick into the ground when it's clear they're not a playoff contender, but it's still unusual to hear Love talking about how it has already been a long year when the Cardinals still have 13 games to go.

With 2:23 left on Sunday, the Texans scored to take a 30-27 lead. A defense that was expected to be one of the best in the NFL could win the game with one stop, or at least make sure the game went to overtime by holding Dallas to a field goal. The Cowboys went downfield and scored a touchdown.

Dallas has a good offense but Houston was supposed to have a good defense. The Texans don't. They are surprisingly average: 14th in DVOA after Sunday's games and 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) allowed per play. Defensive dominance can vary more season to season than offensive excellence, but it's still surprising that the Texans are winless and a middle-of-the-road defense is a big reason for that.

"It sucks, because we know we're the ones out there on the field," Texans cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. said, via the Houston Chronicle . "The coaches put us in the right position to win and we've got to do it. They can't do it, we've got to do it. We've got great coaches, we've got great everybody. We've got to go out there and do our job."

Maybe if Marcus Mariota hadn't gotten injured, the Commanders might have won and been a promising 2-2. They were about to take an early 6-0 lead on the Colts early in the game when Mariota sprained MCL in his right knee. The Commanders' defense played pretty well but Washington's offense couldn't do much with rookie Athan Kaliakmanis in for Mariota and an inactive Jayden Daniels. And 1-3 is a tough hole to dig out of.

With Mariota hurt and the Commanders in danger of having their season slip away further, there has to be tremendous urgency for Daniels to return from a dislocated left elbow.

"That's the hope for us for sure, Jay coming back," Commanders coach Dan Quinn said . "He'll have a full week of practice Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. That's the goal: that he could get into that space."

The Packers won. They faced an undrafted rookie quarterback making his first start and escaped with a 17-14 victory when the Buccaneers threw incomplete on fourth-and-11 from the Packers' 47-yard line. That's not exactly the dominant performance that will get Packers fans off Matt LaFleur's back.

But a win is a win. Green Bay comes home and plays the Bears in Week 5 , a game that was flexed out of the late afternoon time slot in part because of Caleb Williams' injury but also because the Packers aren't that interesting. A third straight loss to the Bears, including last season's horrid collapse in the wild-card round, will have Green Bay fans again calling for LaFleur's job.

It seemed like the Saints were off to a promising start to this season after the second half of last season went very well. But it doesn't look as good after Monday night's blowout loss to the Falcons. New Orleans is a fourth-quarter comeback against the Ravens from being 0-4. Its offensive line did a poor job protecting quarterback Tyler Shough, the running game without injured Travis Etienne Jr. was ineffective and the defense was picked apart by the Falcons.

The one concern about taking the Saints' hot finish to last season and projecting it to this season was that it came against weak competition. In Shough's starts last season, the Saints faced just one team with a winning record, and they lost that game 34-10 to the Rams. Almost beating the Lions and then defeating the Ravens made it look like the Saints would carry over their hot streak from last season. After blowing a game to the Raiders at home and being blown out by the Falcons, it looks more like that start was a mirage, and last season's second half was a product of a soft part of the schedule.

The Colts might have been lucky that the Commanders played most of Sunday's game in London with a third-string rookie quarterback. They did not play well. Daniel Jones' struggles are a real issue. He is 27th among 32 NFL quarterbacks in EPA per play. He is generating -0.065 EPA per play this season. His mark last season was 0.220, which was seventh among all QBs with at least 100 snaps. On Sunday, Jones had just 143 yards against one of the NFL's worst secondaries. He also had an interception and a lost fumble.

Injuries at receiver have been an issue. Missing Alec Pierce changes how defenses approach the Colts, without the threat of big plays downfield. Still, Jones looks much worse than he did last season and it's fair to wonder if his Achilles tear plays a part in that. He still has the support of Colts head coach Shane Steichen, who said Jones is doing a good job.

"I think he's done some really good things and then some things we need to clean up," Steichen told the media . "But he's made some big-time throws."

The days of this Steelers defense scaring anyone are probably over. Pittsburgh is 15th in defensive DVOA through Sunday's games, 14th in EPA allowed per play, 23rd in success rate allowed and 13th in yards per game allowed. Pittsburgh allowed Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson to go 14-of-17 passing for 181 yards and a touchdown in the first half last Thursday night, then let him put together a game-winning drive.

It's just an average defense. The Steelers had the second-oldest defense in the NFL coming into the season by average age, so it's not like there's an obvious turnaround coming with a young unit. The offense's upside is limited with a 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers at quarterback. The ceiling is not very high for this team.

Cleveland should be happy to be on a three-game winning streak. It's probably not sustainable. The Browns have had three very close wins, with the go-ahead scores coming with 3:51, 1:48 and 10 seconds to play. Their point differential is -14. Their DVOA is 23rd.

And still, it's OK to be excited. The young cast around the quarterback position is flashing a lot of talent. Rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion Jr. already look good, and second-year tight end Harold Fannin Jr. is playing well again this season. Deshaun Watson is still very unlikely to be the long-term answer at quarterback but if the Browns get that right in the 2027 NFL Draft, the future is bright. And the Browns are at the Jets next, so a 4-1 start is possible.

"This ain't the old Browns," Cleveland defensive end Jared Verse said, according to Cleveland.com . "We've got new swag."

Detroit's defense isn't good enough to make the Lions scary to anyone. Detroit is allowing 423.8 yards per game, and no other NFL team is giving up more than 392.3. Detroit has allowed 127 points, most in the NFL. On Sunday against the Panthers, Tetairoa McMillan torched the secondary for 192 yards and two touchdowns on 14 catches.

It's bad enough that head coach Dan Campbell was asked afterward if defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard could be relieved of his duties.

"I'm not talking about all that," Campbell told the media after Sunday's loss . "I'm talking about getting better right now, with what we've got, and that's what we're going to do. We're going to find a way to get better with what we've got."

Campbell might not want to talk about it, but the Lions aren't going anywhere with a defense this bad.

Bryce Young is having an unexpected breakout. It's not like Young didn't have talent. He was a Heisman Trophy winner and a No. 1 overall draft pick. But Young has gone from a low-volume quarterback who topped out at 3,011 passing yards in 16 games last season to the NFL's leader in passing yards through Sunday's games. He is averaging 317 passing yards per game, which would be 5,389 through 17 games. That would be the third-most passing yards in a single season in NFL history. Before this season Young had never averaged more than 188.2 yards per game over a full season. Young had three 300-yard games in his first three seasons, and he already has two through four games this season. It's unusual to have a quarterback take that big a leap in his fourth season.

He's off to such a hot start that the Sunday night television audience heard Panthers fans chanting "MVP" at their quarterback.

"Yeah, I heard it," Young said, via the Panthers' site. "In the moment, you're just focusing on executing and trying to move the team."

The Giants are winning and that's a testament to a much-improved coaching staff and some of the young talent. It'll be hard to keep it going. Jameis Winston had two turnovers and took four sacks in a win against a bad Cardinals team that came down to the final play. Winston has started 91 games in his career and has 116 interceptions. Everyone knows where this is headed. And those thinking J.J. McCarthy will be a big improvement haven't seen McCarthy play enough.

Still, the Giants are leading the NFC East. They needed an interception in their end zone with 17 seconds left to beat an 0-4 Titans team two weeks ago, and an interception at the 2-yard line on the final play to beat a 1-3 Cardinals team on Sunday. Both of those games were at home. But head coach John Harbaugh views the high-wire wins as a positive.

"That's what winning is," Harbaugh said, via the team's site . "That's what winning teams do. They find ways to win games. That's why they're winning teams and I'm proud of those guys for that."

It appears the first two games of the Falcons' season shouldn't count for much. The Falcons were down to their third option at quarterback and struggled badly with Cooper Rush running the offense. They went 0-2. If we just judge the Falcons since Michael Penix Jr. came back, then this ranking might be a little low. Atlanta looks like a completely different team. The Falcons have two prime-time, road blowout wins since Penix returned. They pounded the Packers in Week 3, winning 35-14, and then looked even better blasting the Saints on Monday night . The offense that looked so bad has taken off. It's not because Penix has been otherworldly, but he has been solid and defenses have to respect the Falcons' run game in a way they didn't when Rush was at quarterback. The Falcons' defense has been much better the last two weeks too. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich is a big reason the Falcons had a fantastic pass rush against Tyler Shough on Monday night. Maybe the NFC South will have a champion with a winning record after all.

The Eagles still haven't looked good this season. Barely beating the Commanders and Titans, who are a combined 1-7, isn't aging well. They were blown out by the Bears in Week 3 and then on Sunday blew a 10-point lead in the final five minutes. The Eagles did not score in the second half, the second straight game in which they were shut out after halftime. The Eagles were without receiver DeVonta Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, who were inactive, and without running back Saquon Barkley for most of the game after he injured his hamstring. The Eagles also played without right tackle Lane Johnson, who was suddenly ruled out due to a personal matter on Sunday morning. It wouldn't be a surprise if Barkley misses some time, and there is no indication of what's going on with Johnson.

Despite all the excuses, the Eagles still have to be better than they were Sunday. They had 172 yards and went 0-for-12 on third downs. They averaged a putrid 3 yards per play. Jalen Hurts had 10 passing yards on 2 for 9 passing in the second half, which is stunningly bad no matter the opponent or injuries elsewhere.

"It hasn't been good enough," said Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni, who is getting a lot of heat in Philadelphia, according to the team's site .

The Broncos have played eight halves of football. They've been bad for six of them, particularly on offense. On Sunday, against a 49ers defense dealing with many injuries, Denver didn't score its first touchdown until 4:05 remained in the game. The Broncos are now 26th in offense in success rate. Denver is averaging 3.6 yards per rushing attempt, and only four teams are worse. The Broncos average 6.1 yards per pass attempt, and only three teams are worse than that.

The easy switch would be Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb. In Payton's first 18 seasons as a head coach between the Saints and Broncos, his offenses finished outside of the top 15 in yardage and points just three times. They're 27th in yardage and 26th in points scored this season. Payton declined to commit to a play-calling change in the aftermath of the latest offensive dud.

"It's too early," Payton said after Sunday's loss , according to transcripts. "It's a fair question; I appreciate it. It's tough to discuss any of that right now."

One big win changed the scope of the Patriots' season. They're right back in the AFC East race after beating the Bills. Drake Maye went from being berated for his poor play to a 269-yard, three-touchdown day. Receiver Romeo Doubs, who was looking like a free-agency bust after three games, made his impact with two touchdowns. A defense that hadn't been great did a good job limiting Josh Allen, and coming up with an interception with 1:05 to go and the Bills trailing by just three points.

One win, even one as crucial as Sunday's road victory, doesn't eliminate all concerns. But it's better than being three games behind Buffalo already this season.

"It gets us back in the race," head coach Mike Vrabel said, via the team's site . "We knew it was going to be a battle. Josh is unbelievable. Drake went toe-to-toe with him."

CeeDee Lamb had a game for the ages Sunday. He had 17 catches, and only six times in NFL history has a player had more. Lamb had 189 yards, making him the only Cowboy to have 17 catches and 170 yards in a game. He also caught the game-winning touchdown against the Texans with 40 seconds left.

"CeeDee's been great," QB Dak Prescott said., via the team's site .

Dallas still has a big defensive problem. The Cowboys are 31st in EPA allowed per play and there's a big gap between them and the Bills at No. 30. But the offense has mostly been as good as expected. And with the rest of the issues around the NFC East, Dallas is looking like the best team in the division.

The Bengals were off to such a good start at 2-0. And yet the Bengals still aren't over their slow starts. They lost to a flawed Steelers team and then couldn't pull off a late win against the Jaguars at home, dropping them to 2-2. This is the fifth straight season the Bengals have failed to be above .500 through four games.

The running game hasn't been helping. The Bengals have just 297 rushing yards through four games. Only the Packers are worse. They had to abandon it early Sunday. Cincinnati threw it 54 times and had just 12 rushing attempts by running backs. Chase Brown had just 10 yards on nine carries so it's not like the Bengals could trust the run game to sustain the offense. Brown has been productive since his 2024 breakout so it's likely he's just off to a slow start, like the Bengals as a team yet again.

Hindsight changes perceptions, but the Raiders taking a field goal off the board in the third quarter due to a defensive penalty and then failing to convert on fourth-and-2 was a critical turning point in a three-point loss to the Chiefs.

"We were going to be aggressive going into the game," Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said, according to the team's site . "I don't regret it. I regret not getting it."

Overall, the Raiders acquitted themselves just fine in defeat. They led with less than four minutes to play. They might have answered a late Chiefs touchdown, but they lost a fumble on the next kickoff. Las Vegas outgained the Chiefs 437-398, which is of little consolation but shows Vegas was close to knocking off Kansas City. If anything, the Raiders validated their hot start with a close loss to a Chiefs team that is 4-0 and has won nine of the last 10 AFC West titles.

The Vikings did something Sunday that no other team has accomplished since 1923. It's not great though. They're the first team since the 1923 Chicago Cardinals to start 4-0 and not score a touchdown in two of the wins.

The Vikings' offense has not been good. Not having Kyler Murray for a full game and most of a second is a reasonable excuse, as is missing Justin Jefferson for almost two full games. We'll see if the offense looks much better with Jefferson back and Murray healthy. But Murray hasn't been a very good NFL quarterback; the woebegone Cardinals took a dead salary cap hit of $54.7 million to be done with him. Even without Jefferson the Vikings should score at least one touchdown against a bad Dolphins defense at home (yes, T.J. Hockenson held up after getting a game-clinching first down when he could have scored, that's noted). Murray is last among NFL quarterbacks in success rate and second-to-last in EPA per play. Minnesota is going to take a step back if the offense doesn't get better, no matter how good the defense is.

It's tough to drop the Rams two spots after a road win against Philadelphia, but it's getting to a point where they have to play better to reclaim their status as an unquestionably elite team. The first three-plus quarters Sunday were ugly on offense. And that was with Puka Nacua back. Matthew Stafford has six touchdowns and six interceptions in four games. He had eight interceptions all of last season. Stafford is 38 years old and many quarterbacks see a steep decline in their late 30s, if they're still playing.

The Rams won because their defense was fantastic and then the offense came alive for two clutch drives at the end. A decision by the Eagles to go for it on fourth down instead of taking a short field goal to make the score 23-10 in the fourth quarter helped too. The Rams found a way to win but they've looked good in only one of four games, and that was after the Giants lost quarterback Jaxson Dart to injury in the first quarter. It doesn't get easier either: The Rams host the Bills next Monday night.

Everything is on hold as the Ravens find out if Lamar Jackson is OK from an ankle injury. Presumably, he was sitting in the second half mostly as a precaution, as the Ravens led 24-7 against a terrible Titans team. But any injury to Jackson's lower body is a concern considering how dangerous he is on the move.

Overall there's nothing wrong with the Ravens holding on to beat the Titans after they went in a shell without Jackson, though 13 penalties need to be addressed. They did enough to win, despite being outscored 11-0 in the second half, and that's all that matters. They didn't move down in these rankings as much as the Bears and Jaguars moved up past them. The Ravens are still a Super Bowl contender. But that depends on Jackson staying healthy. We saw in the second half what the Ravens would look like without Jackson, and it's not pretty.

The Bears get a big bump, and it's because of their defense. Chicago had a bad Week 1 on defense, and that seemed to be in line with its preseason expectations. The Bears were 25th in defensive DVOA last season and didn't make major improvements in the offseason. But over the last three weeks the Bears' defense has been excellent. From Week 2 through Week 4 they are third in EPA allowed per play. The only touchdowns they've given up in three weeks was an Eagles quarterback sneak that was snapped barely before time ran out in the first half, and a garbage time touchdown to the Jets in the fourth quarter when they led 23-6.

It helps that Chicago has faced the Vikings with Carson Wentz, an Eagles offense that looks surprisingly inept and the Jets, but the results are impressive. If Chicago has an above-average defense, this is a Super Bowl contender. We all know the offense will be fine, especially when Caleb Williams returns.

The Bills could have essentially finished the AFC East race. They were at home against the Patriots and could have exited that game with a three-game lead in the division. That's what made Sunday's loss a disappointment. Buffalo's defense in particular let down, allowing 405 yards to a New England offense that had been struggling.

Buffalo's offense is just fine, as it always will be with Josh Allen. Though Allen himself cost the team with an interception in the final two minutes that he admitted he should have thrown away instead of taking a risk downfield. The Bills' defense is the bigger issue. It is now 30th in EPA per play allowed and 26th in DVOA. The lowest a Super Bowl champion has ever ranked in defensive DVOA is the 2006 Colts at 25th. Either the Bills' defense needs to improve or Buffalo is in danger of wasting another season of Allen's prime.

The transitive property doesn't really work in the NFL but consider this: In Week 3, the Jaguars beat the Patriots 35-6. A week later that same Patriots team beat the Bills on the road. The easy takeaway from that, and how Jacksonville has looked in a season-plus of the Liam Coen era: The Jaguars have been underrated here and that needs to change. Coen is 16-5 as Jaguars head coach.

Jacksonville is second to San Francisco in DVOA , and that seems like the right spot. The Jags have blown out the Browns and Patriots, who are 5-1 against everyone else. They won at the Bengals, who had started the season 2-0 and are considered dangerous. The loss to the Broncos was unfortunate, but Jacksonville led 10-3 at halftime and it's not the first team to fade in the second half at altitude early in the season. Had it not been for that second half at Denver, Jacksonville would have a case to be the No. 1 team in these rankings. The Jaguars are very good.

If you want the Chiefs to fall off sometime soon, it's probably not going to happen. Their upcoming schedule is soft and should lead to a start of 8-2 or better:

Week 5: bye Week 6: vs. Chargers Week 7: at Seahawks Week 8: at Broncos Week 9: vs. Jets Week 10: at Falcons Week 11: vs. Cardinals

That's four games in which Kansas City should be significant favorites, and while the game at the Seahawks will be very tough, it's not like the Broncos are playing great. That's a winnable road game. A 4-2 run through those six games seems to be the worst outcome. The Chiefs aren't going away.

The Seahawks have been far from perfect. It was disappointing that they relaxed so much after taking a 27-6 lead against the Chargers that their defense had to get a stop in the final two minutes after Los Angeles cut the lead to 30-23. And it wasn't ideal that Seattle lost in Week 3 to the Commanders, who are 0-3 in their other games this season.

But there shouldn't be much concern about the Seahawks. The loss to the Commanders was fluky (they outgained Washington by 179 yards) and they won their other three games. The defense is still spectacular, ranking first in DVOA, even if it let up against the Chargers for a bit. Next up is a battle against the 49ers that likely will determine who is No. 1 in the Power Rankings after Week 5.

"Got to look forward, move forward. Got a big week ahead of us, and guys are excited," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said, according to the team's site. "They played extremely hard, stayed together, and did enough to win the game, so we're thankful."

It has been a good runout for the 49ers. They haven't played a true road game yet. They faced the Cardinals and Dolphins, two of the NFL's worst teams. The weirdness of the Australia trip for the Rams has been talked about often. But the 49ers just keep winning and looking pretty good doing it.

If there's any remaining skepticism about the 49ers, this week will be telling. San Francisco plays at Seattle on Sunday afternoon. San Francisco's offense is first in the NFL in EPA per play and by a wide margin (0.274 with the Bills in second at 0.204). If the 49ers can keep that going against an excellent Seahawks defense, it will solidify the 49ers as the No. 1 team in the NFL so far this season.

articles.title: “Sometimes you report things teams don’t want you to report”: Ian Rapoport reveals Ben Johnson’s ploy to mislead teams over Chicago Bears starter
articles.summary: Ben Johnson is a first-time head coach. He led the Chicago Bears to an 11-6 season record in 2025. He also led the team to first place in the NFC North.
articles.body: Ben Johnson is a first-time head coach. He led the Chicago Bears to an 11-6 season record in 2025. He also led the team to first place in the NFC North. The Bears won the 2025 NFC North division title.Caleb Williams was unstoppable under Ben Johnson’s guidance: 3,900+ yards, 27 touchdowns, and 7 interceptions. Johnson probably intends to carry that same approach into his second year as the first-time head coach of Chicago. How does he do that? By not revealing who his starting quarterback is!Now, his 2026 chapter brought a calamity he didn't have in 2025: Caleb Williams got injured.Williams took care of himself throughout the 2025 season. But two games into the 2026 season, he rekindled a college injury: a grade 2 hamstring. This must have left Ben Johnson looking for different ways to trick other teams. How does he do that? NFL insider Ian Rapoport revealed just hours ago to everyone!Ian Rapoport reveals Ben Johnson’s ploy to mislead teams over Bears starterWeek 1 starter: Caleb Williams. Week 2: Caleb Williams. Week 3: With Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent both injured, Case Keenum started. Week 4: Ben Johnson declined to name the starter. Analysts reported that Tyson Bagent would start.But just to stir things up, Case Keenum showed up for the first snap while Tyson Bagent lined up at receiver. What happened next? Keenum quietly left the gridiron and Bagent led the team to a Week 4 victory over the New York Jets.“Well, I got all these memos saying that Tyson was starting before I ever made an announcement, so I wanted to get Case out there,” said Johnson. “It was like his ceremonial first pitch out there. Handing off the torch.”Or, it could also mean that the coach wanted to carry forward Case Keenum’s luck factor! That helped the Chicago Bears win the Week 3 game over the much-dreaded Philadelphia Eagles. You never know.Now that Week 5 is here and reports about who’s going to start in Chicago have already started puzzling media houses and other NFL teams, NFL insider Ian Rapoport has revealed Ben Johnson’s ploy very conveniently.Tyson Bagent expected to start against Green BayNFL insider Ian Rapoport reported just hours ago that Tyson Bagent is expected to start at quarterback for the Chicago Bears against the Green Bay Packers in Week 5. Caleb Williams remains away from his return. He could return to practice next week. Ian Rapoport later revealed Ben Johnson’s ploy.The head coach had previously avoided confirming Tyson Bagent as the starter. Instead, the coach very cunningly used Case Keenum at quarterback and Tyson Bagent at receiver on the opening snap of the Week 4 game. This little stunt could technically help the coach say that both quarterbacks were starters.Ian Rapoport praised Ben Johnson’s good-natured handling of the QB starter situation. He noted that teams sometimes try to hide information from reporters.So clues don’t reach opponents to help them decide on a specific QB-based game plan!“Okay, so this week, and I say this week very specifically, Tyson Bagent is expected to start at quarterback for the Chicago Bears. Seems like Caleb Williams is still a couple of weeks away. So not going to play this week. Perhaps able to practice next week,” said Ian Rapoport via NFL Network.“The reason I say that so specifically since last week, there was a lot of reporting by me and some others as well that Tyson Bagent would be the starter.Ben Johnson declined to say that that was the case, and then the first snap happened, and you had Case Keenum at starting quarterback, but Tyson Bagent at receiver - just so Ben Johnson could say, ‘Look, I said I would start both quarterbacks. I said, I consider them both starters. Look, they're both starters.’And I will say, as someone who covers this and knows this, that sometimes you can report things the teams don't want you to report. I very much appreciated the good-natured way that Ben Johnson handled this and also kind of funny, really.”Long story short: Tyson Bagent is expected to start Week 5 against the Green Bay Packers. But we never know; maybe Case Keenum will come back and stay for the game this time? articles.title: Why did the NFL rescind Kyle Juszczyk’s $14,926 fine after calling his 49ers celebration a beer chug
articles.summary: Kyle Juszczyk was fined $14,926 for a celebration the NFL believed showed him chugging beer.
articles.body: Kyle Juszczyk was fined $14,926 for a celebration the NFL believed showed him chugging beer. Two weeks later, the league decided it had read the moment wrong.The San Francisco 49ers fullback won his appeal after arguing that the celebration referenced his longtime “Juice” nickname. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Wednesday that the NFL rescinded the fine after determining Juszczyk was simulating drinking from a juice box.Why did the NFL rescind Kyle Juszczyk’s $14,926 celebration fine?The issue began during San Francisco’s Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sept. 20.Juszczyk used the celebration twice during the game, including after a 6-yard touchdown. The NFL fined him Sept. 23 for “engaging in offensive demonstrations,” according to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner.The league believed Juszczyk had performed an “imitation of chugging a beer.”Juszczyk immediately disputed that interpretation.His nickname has been “Juice” for years, and he regularly celebrates by mimicking drinking juice. He even has a juice box printed on one of his thigh pads.During a Sept. 24 media session, Juszczyk placed a jug marked “Not Beer” near his locker while explaining the celebration.“When I celebrate, I celebrate by drinking juice and it’s been that way for years,” Juszczyk said.He also challenged the logic of the punishment even under the NFL’s original interpretation.“Even if it was beer, I don't think that should be a problem with all the beer endorsements that we have in the NFL,” Juszczyk said. “We have everything. So even if it was beer, which it wasn't, I still felt like it wasn't an infraction.”Juszczyk took the same argument into his appeal.Schefter reported Wednesday that the league withdrew the fine “because his celebration was simulating drinking a juice box, not a beer.”The league’s explanation also referenced Juszczyk’s argument that the punishment was hypocritical because of the NFL’s Bud Light sponsorships.That distinction matters. The NFL did not simply reduce the penalty. It determined that the action it had punished was not what Juszczyk was doing in the first place.What does Kyle Juszczyk’s reversal mean for the NFL’s other drinking celebration fines?Juszczyk’s successful appeal creates an obvious question about similar fines.NBC Sports reported that Indianapolis Colts guard Matt Goncalves was also fined for mimicking a drinking celebration. As of Wednesday, there had been no reported change to his punishment.That does not mean the two cases will receive the same outcome. Juszczyk had a specific defense tied to his nickname, his previous celebrations and the juice-box imagery he already uses.His case also produced an unexpected result away from the league office.According to ESPN, multiple brands contacted Juszczyk after the fine became public. Ocean Spray later signed him to a partnership and announced plans to give away 14,926 bottles of juice, matching the exact dollar amount of the rescinded fine.The number that originally represented Juszczyk’s punishment is now part of a sponsorship campaign built around the same celebration.For the NFL, the appeal closed one dispute but left the broader policy under a brighter light. Juszczyk argued that his celebration was about juice. articles.title: Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson's Fine For 'Imitation of Shotgunning a Beer' Rescinded by NFL After Appeal
articles.summary: The NFL and NFLPA's joint appeals officer overturned the $13,611 fine levied to Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson for the "imitation of shotgunning a beer," according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The NFL and NFLPA's joint appeals officer overturned the $13,611 fine levied to Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson for the "imitation of shotgunning a beer," according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Ferguson appealed on the basis he was simulating the drinking of Gatorade, not an alcoholic beverage.

The two-time Pro Bowler hauled in a 10-yard touchdown pass from Dak Prescott in the second quarter of a 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 2. He gestured toward fellow tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford, and they had a joint celebration that seemingly didn't leave a lot of room for interpretation.

NFL suspends two refs for 'unprofessional conduct'

There was apparently enough evidence for Ferguson to convince the appeals officer otherwise.

San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk was fined for making a similar gesture. His appeal was also successful as he argued he was motioning drinking from a juice box as a reference to his "Juice" nickname.

Ferguson is earning a little more than $8 million for the 2026 season, so a $13,611 fine would've been a drop in the bucket. Still, he felt the need to set the record straight.

articles.title: Keldon Johnson's KJ Kares bringing Thanksgiving drive back to San Antonio
articles.summary: Spurs forward and reigning Sixth Man of the Year Keldon Johnson is bringing his KJ Kares Thanksgiving Drive back to San Antonio on Nov. 21.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs forward Keldon Johnson is bringing his Thanksgiving tradition back to the Alamo City.

Johnson, the reigning NBA Sixth Man of the Year, will host a Thanksgiving drive in San Antonio on Nov. 21 through his KJ Kares foundation. The event continues his efforts to support local families during the holiday season.

"Giving back to the city that has given Keldon so much has always been close to his heart," KJ Kares said in an Instagram post announcing the event.

"We're so excited to come together this Thanksgiving season to support local families and our community."

The location, time and information for families interested in attending have not yet been announced.

KJ Kares is also seeking sponsors and community partners for the drive. The organization said it has heard from potential partners and plans to share more information about sponsorships and partnerships soon.

Those interested in becoming sponsors or community partners can contact KJ Kares through its social media account and include an email address or other contact information.

"More details coming soon," the organization said. "We can't wait to bring this one home."

Johnson is coming off a standout season. He was named the 2025-26 Kia NBA Sixth Man of the Year after averaging 13.2 points and 5.4 rebounds in all 82 regular-season games, all off the bench. He also set a Spurs single-season record with 1,081 points as a reserve.

Johnson is the second Spurs player to win the award, joining Manu Ginobili, who received it in 2007-08.

The Spurs selected Johnson with the 29th overall pick in the 2019 NBA Draft. He has spent his entire NBA career with San Antonio.

articles.title: Ravens fans, media react to blockbuster trade for Cam Jurgens
articles.summary: Ravens fans celebrated the arrival of Cam Jurgens while NFL observers debated the substantial draft price Baltimore paid
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens answered their offensive-line emergency with one of the NFL season's biggest trades, acquiring two-time Pro Bowl lineman Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Philadelphia Eagles , according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Reaction across social media centered on two competing ideas. Ravens fans welcomed an established blocker who can stabilize a position depleted by three injured centers, while others questioned Baltimore's decision to surrender a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round selection for a player currently in concussion protocol and carrying a contract that becomes considerably more expensive after this season.

articles.title: NFL all-free agency team: Kenneth Walker and the 15 best signings, trades in 2026 (so far)
articles.summary: Which newcomers have had the most significant impact for their new teams?
articles.body:
The NFL offseason is different from that of other sports. Sometimes it takes just calculated spending on players to change a team, with quality becoming a lot more important than quantity. The key is getting good return on investment in free agency, whether a veteran is acquired through signing or trade.

The teams that worekd well in the open market in 2026 and seeing the fruits of their labor with results early in the 2026 regular season. Starting with the two best teams in the AFC West and getting into the rest, here's looking at who's provided the most significant impact through the quarter term.

The Raiders waited until April, weeks before drafting Fernando Mendoza No.1 overall, to sign Cousins. Some scoffed at them giving him a five-year, $172 million deal, but in reality, they got a break from the Falcons . Las Vegas is on the hook for only $11.3 million in guaranteed money, with Atlanta still paying Cousins $8.7 million.

There also was skepticism of new offensive-minded coach Klint Kubiak sticking to his word and sitting in Mendoza and starting Cousins. No one is questioning that plan now with Cousins producing so well in the system, a big reason for the surprise 3-1 start. Mendoza might get rookie starts later, but those might come only if the Raiders fade out of the playoff picture or Cousins gets hurt.

Running back: Kenneth Walker III, Chiefs

Walker gets the unofficial award for free-agent pickup of the year. He's not the first Super Bowl MVP (Larry Brown, anyone?) to parlay that into a big contract elsewhere. The Chiefs splurged on him quickly with a three-year, $45 million deal to take him away from the Seahawks .

Through four games before the Chiefs' Week 5 bye, Walker leads the NFL with 537 rushing yards, averaging 134.3 yards per game and and also a league-high 6.2 yards per carry. He also has six combined TDs and leads everyone with his 621 scrimmage yards.

There's no doubt Walker has provided the needed ingredient to get the Chiefs' offense back on track: A power running game to take pressure off Patrick Mahomes and better open up the passing game. Walker, even if he cools down a bit from that hot start, will keep providing critical balance and explosiveness.

Given Evans' age (33), the 49ers got him to leave the Buccaneers after 12 seasons on a reasonable three-year, $42.5 million deal. Although he's battled injury during the Niners ' 4-0 start, he has played in every game, catching 17 of 24 targets for 213 yards and 2 TDs.

Those numbers aren't big, but the impact of his downfield and red zone presence has been important in facilitating matchups for Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and Deebo Samuel. Evans remains dangerous in goal-to-go situations and some point, and once healthier, he'll deliver more to match the elite deep passing of Brock Purdy.

WEEK 5 PREDICTIONS: Against the spread | Straight up

Likely has had a hot start for the Giants , who signed him to a three-year $40 million deal in March so he would follow his former Ravens coach John Harbaugh to New York. He was big right away with Jaxson Dart, as his 8 catches for 72 yards and 2 TDs was key to taking down the rival Cowboys in Week 1.

After a couple of games struggling to connect with Dart injury replacement Jameis Winston, Likely had 7 catches for 66 yards to help beat the Cardinals in Week 4. He'll remain an important factor playing off star No. 1 receiver Malik Nabers.

Offensive tackle: Rasheed Walker, Panthers

Walker hasn't been a top-flight blocker, but it's difficult to find left tackles in free agency. The former Packer has at least solidified a key position, along with rookie first-round tackle Monroe Freeling, while both Ikem Ekonwu and Taylor Moton are out with injuries. There should be some credit for protecting Bryce Young, who leads the NFL with 1,268 passing yards through Week 4.

The Raiders couldn't keep Parham at guard after breaking the bank for new center Tyler Linderbaum. The Jets took advantage by signing him to a two-year, $20 million deal as part of their massive offensive overhaul. Parham has been strong all-around on the left side.

The Lions lost Frank Ragnow to retirement after the 2024 season but have found a potential long-term answer in '26. When Detroit traded running back David Mongtomery to Houston, they acquired Scruggs and two draft picks. Scruggs has fit in well blocking for a prolific running now featuring Jahmyr Gibbs without Montgomery.

Defensive tackle: Dexter Lawrence, Bengals

Knowing they would lose Trey Hendrickson in free agency, the Bengals had to make a corresponding move to help their defensive line. That came via trading No. 10 overall pick to the Giants to address the inside. He has three sacks to keep up his dominant inside pass rush and also has helped vs. the run.

Mafe also left the Super Bowl champion Seahawks to become a more regular pass rusher in Cincinnati, signing a three-year, $60 million deal. Maye has a couple of sacks for defensive coordinator Al Golden, who now has replenished talent to better execute his scheme.

The Raiders also spent well on defense, getting Dean from the Eagles on a three-year, $36 million deal. In four games, Dean leads the league with 3 forced fumbles. He has 1.5 sacks and has been great in coverage over the middle. He's doing everything for defensive coordinator Rob Leonard, including giving Maxx Crosby a co-leader on the field.

McDuffie has been much better than their other new starter, fellow former Chief Jaylen Watson. The Rams needed McDuffie to be a dominant cover man after giving up four draft picks to acquire him from Kansas City, including No. 29 in the first round in '26. He's been a shutdown force in coverage with a league-high 7 passes defended and an interception.

Fitzpatrick was acquired in a rare intra-divisoin trade with the Jets giving up only a seventh-round pick to get him. New York then gave him a three-year, $40 million extension. The former Steeler has become a star again in Aaron Glenn's secondary since healthy for the past two games. He ended the Jets' 20-game interception drought in Week 4 vs. the Bears.

Stout has a great last name given the strength of his leg. He joined Likely and a few others in making the move from Baltimore with Harbaugh after getting a three-year, $12.5 million contract. Stout is averaging 50.6 yards per punt and has put 9 of his 20 attempts inside the 20.

Gay has gone 10-for-10 on field goals, behind only the Vikings' Will Reichard (12-for-12) and the Colts' Spencer Shrader (11-for-11). He's made all 9 of his extra point tries and 6 of his field goals have come from 40 yards or longer. Not bad for a guy making only $1.6 million on a one-year deal.

The former Chiefs and 49ers wide receiver was signed to a modest one-year, $2.5 million contract. With Jayden Reed going down again with injury, Moore has been huge on both punts and kickoffs. He has averaged 16.0 yards on punt returns (No. 2 in the league) and been solid with 27.6 yards per kickoff return.

articles.title: Sauce Gardner Says He Gave 'Unacceptable' Effort in Colts' Win vs. Commanders
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner owned up to his poor showing in the team's 30-13 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 4.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner owned up to his poor showing in the team's 30-13 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 4.

Gardner told reporters Wednesday that his effort level was "unacceptable" and "an embarrassing watch."

Commanders quarterbacks Athan Kaliakmanis and Marcus Mariota combined to throw for 217 yards and one touchdown. Kaliakmanis, who replaced an injured Mariota, went 15-of-33 through the air.

It's not like Washington lit up the Colts secondary for 60 minutes.

But Gardner got beat deep on a couple of throws. Kaliakmanis hit Treylon Burks for a 47-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter and then found Dyami Brown for a 48-yard completion on the next drive.

According to Pro Football Reference , Gardner was targeted seven times and allowed 104 yards on three completions. Those numbers don't reflect the totality of his performance, either.

Antonio Williams' 87-yard touchdown reception was wiped off the board, but that doesn't let Gardner off the hook for a poor pursuit angle and a general lack of effort in trying to chase down the rookie wideout.

Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo came to Gardner's defense somewhat.

"Does Sauce want those couple of plays back? Sure," he said, per the Indianapolis Star 's Nathan Brown . "But is it all on Sauce on those particular plays? No."

Anarumo went on to say Burks' touchdown catch was somewhat fluky and partially the result of good fortune for Washington.

"It was a very, very unusual play, because you had a rookie quarterback and a receiver kind of not on the same page — one expecting the back shoulder (throw), and the other one not throwing it," he said.

Gardner is going to be scrutinized closely in every single game he plays for the Colts given the cost to acquire him. Indianapolis sent two first-round picks to the New York Jets and assumed the four-year, $120 million extension the two-time All-Pro signed with his old team.

Roughly a year on, the Colts don't look like winners from the blockbuster deal.

Even elite stars can experience a game to forget. In the case of Gardner, his showing in Week 4 was part of a larger, more concerning pattern.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Takes J.J. McCarthy's Old Vikings Jersey Number After Practice Squad Contract
articles.summary: There's a new No. 9 on the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
There's a new No. 9 on the Minnesota Vikings.

Veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. will be wearing No. 9 after signing Wednesday with the Vikings' practice squad.

No. 9 was most recently worn in Minnesota by quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who was traded to the Giants Sept. 28. McCarthy is wearing No. 18 with his new team.

Beckham opened the season with the Giants before he was released by the team Sept. 29.

He played 19 offensive snaps and received three targets with no catches before he was let go. Head coach John Harbaugh said after his departure the Giants hadn't been "getting enough" out of the veteran wideout.

Beckham started out his NFL career wearing No. 13 while recording three consecutive Pro Bowl campaigns with the Giants.

He also wore No. 13 after joining the Cleveland Browns before later donning No. 3 with the Los Angeles Rams, Baltimore Ravens and Miami Dolphins.

Beckham last saw regular-season NFL action for the Dolphins before he was waived by the team in December 2024. He sat out the 2025 season after starting the campaign on a PED suspension .

He made his NFL comeback this offseason with the Giants, wearing No. 3 during training camp and the preseason before switching to No. 13 ahead of his regular-season return.

Quarterback Jake Haener is wearing No. 13 with the Giants following Beckham's release.

The Vikings already had wide receiver Tai Felton wearing No. 13, while star wideout Jordan Addison has claimed No. 3.

Beckham will now hope his new number coincides with a new shot at the NFL as he looks to earn more snaps down the stretch of the season.

articles.title: Dak Prescott, C.J. Stroud's Postgame Conversation Shown in Viral Video After Cowboys' Win vs. Texans
articles.summary: After the Dallas Cowboys' 34-30 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday, quarterbacks Dak Prescott and C.J. Stroud had a brief but interesting interaction.
articles.body:
After the Dallas Cowboys' 34-30 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday, quarterbacks Dak Prescott and C.J. Stroud had a brief but interesting interaction.

The short postgame conversation between Prescott and Stroud went viral this week, as many wondered if there was any extra meaning behind Prescott's advice.

"Just shake it off," Prescott told Stroud. "Go get some wins, bro. Get some wins going, brother."

Of course, the interaction is reminiscent of when Stroud tried to advise Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams after a game two years ago. Stroud, who was the reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year during Williams' first season, came off as if he were trying to "big brother" the 2024 No. 1 pick.

This time around, it was Stroud who needed some encouragement after he and the Texans fell to 0-4. Three of Houston's four losses have come by five points or less.

Stroud and the Texans will try to shake off the disappointing start to the year when they return to action in Week 5 to face the Tennessee Titans, who are also 0-4.

articles.title: Titans' Cam Ward Responds to Controversy After Viral Video of Media Session After Ravens Loss
articles.summary: A video of Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward following his team's 24-18 road loss to the Baltimore Ravens last Sunday went viral after media members hadn't arrived yet at his press conference from the team's open locker room session.
articles.body:
A video of Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward following his team's 24-18 road loss to the Baltimore Ravens last Sunday went viral after media members hadn't arrived yet at his press conference from the team's open locker room session .

On Wednesday, Ward addressed the situation.

"I mean, they talking about that, that's something for them to talk about," Ward said. "If they need something to talk about, we'd rather them talk about that than our performance, so we're just trying to put a good product on the field."

It's been a difficult season for Ward and the Titans, who have lost their first four games. Tennessee has averaged just 13.75 points per game, which is the second-lowest mark in the league. Ward has thrown for just 181.5 passing yards per game and three touchdowns.

The good news is that the defense has fared well overall, as Tennessee has allowed the ninth-fewest PPG (20.8). In theory, an improved offense can go a long way toward the Titans salvaging this season.

Rookie wideout Carnell Tate, the No. 4 overall pick in April's draft, could help. Tate had a breakout Week 4, catching nine passes for 145 yards against the Ravens.

Still, the Titans need to figure things out and fast. Only one team (the 1992 Los Angeles Chargers) has ever made the playoffs after starting 0-4. So right now, one can understand frustrations emanating from Nashville in head coach Robert Saleh's first season.

The Titans will hope to get a win on the board Sunday when they host the winless Houston Texans.

articles.title: NFL swallows $15K fine against 49ers’ Kyle Juszczyk for pretending to chug beer on field
articles.summary: The star fullback, nicknamed “Juice,” had argued he was celebrating a victory over the rival Miami Dolphins by simulating drinking a juice box, not a beer.
articles.body: Star San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk appears to have some serious juice with the NFL. The NFL has rescinded the $14,926 fine it imposed on Juszczyk last month for “engaging in offensive demonstrations” by doing an “imitation of chugging a beer” during his team’s victory over the Miami Dolphins in Week 2 of the current season, a league spokesperson confirmed Wednesday. The NFL backed off the fine after Juszczyk appealed the punishment and argued that he was actually pretending to drink his preferred beverage, namely juice, and that he has been doing that kind of celebration for years. NBC News has reached out to Juszczyk and the 49ers for comment on the NFL’s rescinding of the fine. When the NFL hit Juszczyk with the fine on Sept. 23, it said Juszczyk, a 10-time Pro Bowl fullback, violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1 of its rules against unsportsmanlike conduct. “Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste,” the NFL wrote in its fine letter, ESPN first reported. Juszczyk, who is in his 14th year of pro football, confirmed online that he’d been fined. “Can’t make this stuff up,” he said on X. Later, in a meeting with reporters at the team’s practice facility in Santa Clara, California, Juszczyk, a 35-year-old Harvard graduate, sounded more amused than annoyed by the development. “I don’t know how else to say it: I wasn’t drinking beer in my celebration,” he said. “I think you guys all know my nickname is ‘Juice.’ I have juice on my pads. The stadium yells ‘Juice’ when I catch the ball. When I celebrate, I celebrate by drinking juice, and it’s been the way for years. So I was surprised as anybody when I got a fine this week.” Juszczyk said that when 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan told him about the fine, he thought Shanahan “was just messing with me.” At least nobody is calling Juszczyk “The Juice.” That nickname belonged to San Francisco native O.J. Simpson, the NFL star and accused double murderer, whose initials stood for Orenthal James and is slang for “orange juice.” He died two years ago at age 76 of prostate cancer.

articles.title: The Long Road Back: NFL Ties League History With 5 Winless Teams Through Week 4
articles.summary: There’s a race to the bottom of the NFL standings four games into the season, including two surprisingly winless teams.
articles.body: There's a race to the bottom of the NFL standings four games into the season, including some surprisingly winless teams. A record-tying five teams are 0-4 one month in, marking just the seventh time that has happened in NFL history and the first since 2019. Some of the winless teams aren't too surprising, with Miami there as part of a rebuild in a season when the Dolphins are carrying a record $184 million in dead money charges on the salary cap. Tennessee is winless after back-to-back three-win seasons. The other winless teams are a bit more of a surprise: Tampa Bay is there after coming into the season as the favorite to win the NFC South, while Houston and the Los Angeles Chargers are 0-4 after making the playoffs last season. This is just the third time in NFL history that two teams started a season 0-4 after making the playoffs the previous season. It also happened in 1999 with defending conference champions Atlanta and Denver doing it, and in 1992 with the Los Angeles Raiders and New York Jets both starting 0-4. The Buccaneers have lost four one-score games, with their minus-20 point differential the fifth-best ever for an 0-4 team, and the best since Minnesota was outscored by 19 points over the first four games in 2011. The Chargers haven't been nearly as competitive, getting outscored by 39 points for the second-worst point differential in the league so far. The start for the Texans has been frustrating because they have led in the final 2 minutes in three of the four losses, including a 34-30 loss to Dallas on Sunday when the Cowboys scored the winning touchdown with 40 seconds to play. They are the second team since at least 1991 to lose three times in the first four games after leading in the final 2 minutes. The Chargers did it in 2016. The only other teams in the Super Bowl era to start the season 0-4 despite leading at any point in the fourth quarter in three of the games were the 2013 Bucs and 2011 Vikings. C.J. Stroud is the first quarterback since 1950, when starts were first tracked, to lose the first four games of a season without throwing an interception. Three teams have started the season 4-0, with Kansas City and Minnesota doing it after missing the playoffs in 2025. The last time two teams started 4-0 after missing the playoffs was 2013, when the Chiefs and New Orleans did it. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Grade the trade: What does dealing center Cam Jurgens to Ravens mean for Eagles' Jalen Hurts in short and long run?
articles.summary: The gem of the trade is the 2028 second-rounder, giving the Eagles a surplus of picks. The A.J. Brown trade netted a 2028 first, so they'll be outfitted with...
articles.body:
It has been a busy week for the offensive lines of the Eagles and Ravens. Wednesday's trade between the two teams shuffled things up even more .

The Eagles traded offensive lineman Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Ravens in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.

The timing, one day after longtime Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly announced his retirement , is perhaps the most surprising element of the trade.

The Ravens, who have had a hard time replacing Tyler Linderbaum at center, recently watched as Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic all suffered injuries, forcing 2026 first-rounder Vega Ioane over from guard to center.

Jurgens now figures to be Baltimore's center for multiple seasons, given the nature of his contract after he signed an extension last year.

So who won this fascinating trade? Let's dive into each team's perspective.

Eagles may have eyes on 2028, but short-term worries arise

The Eagles' offensive line was already in rough shape, and Johnson's retirement changed the picture dramatically. So why are the Eagles selling off OL assets?

On the surface, it's hard not to initially wonder if the Eagles are semi-punting on this season. Losing two OL starters in a two-day span, no matter how poorly the unit was playing, is a tough look. Johnson is a future first-ballot Hall of Fame candidate, and the Eagles thought highly enough about Jurgens to sign him to the major extension a little over a year ago.

Things really fell off when Landon Dickerson landed on injured reserve, which necessitated Jurgens moving from center — by far his best position — to guard, where he has struggled this season.

Now, with Johnson retired and Jurgens gone, the line will take on a wholly different look. Left tackle Jordan Mailata is now the one true fixture, although right guard Tyler Steen has appeared to do his job well. Our best guess is that Drew Kendall and Willie Lampkin are the new center and left guard, respectively, although they could also flip spots if needed, and rookie Markel Bell steps in at right tackle.

Dickerson is eligible to return from IR after Week 5, so he also could help solidify things inside. The undersized Lampkin could be the smallest offensive lineman in the NFL, and he has two regular-season offensive snaps — neither of them on the offensive line. Bell played in last season's national title game at Miami and is a massive blocker, but he looked overmatched against the Rams after replacing the injured Johnson.

It's hard not to wonder if the Eagles have worsened the group in the short term with the hope of a long-term return. Yet that payoff could be big.

The gem of the trade is the 2028 second-rounder, giving the Eagles a surplus of picks in what could be a crucial offseason for the franchise. The A.J. Brown trade netted a 2028 first, so they'll be outfitted with four picks in the top 64 that year. This is not some happy accident; this is by design.

That could be the offseason when the Eagles can first move on from Jalen Hurts if they want to, without completely nuking their salary-cap situation. And though it's early, 2028 also could be a banner QB class in the draft, depending on who declares early next spring and who doesn't. Two firsts and two seconds, even with where the Eagles typically pick in the draft, is the kind of ammunition a team must have to be in the running to select a quarterback up high.

Hurts now has this season and next to prove his worth to the team, but he'll arguably be doing it this season with a weakened group up front. That's what the Eagles are willing to live with in the short term, apparently, even with the NFC East still very much up for grabs.

The trade return, contract shedding and general manager Howie Roseman's long-term vision deserve some praise. But the cost now could be great. It's a tricky deal to grade from the Eagles' perspective, with a wide range of possibilities. Splitting the difference is probably the most fair way to judge it — a B+ for the long term and a D+ for this season.

Ravens filled a big need, but was it an overpay?

The Ravens had a clear, glaring need at center, and they solved it. The question is how well.

Jurgens is a two-time Pro Bowler who is theoretically in his prime at age 27. He's played well for the Eagles, but out of need the team moved him to left guard — and the results have been surprisingly bad this season. In addition to pass-blocking issues, Jurgens has had four penalties in four games; he's never had more than six in any of his full seasons prior to this year.

A move back to center figures to help Jurgens, and getting a healthy remainder of the season out of him figures to lift the entire Baltimore front. The rest of the unit had appeared relatively solid through the first four games, but the shaky play at center — and the multiple changes there — had held the unit back.

Jurgens has a fairly lengthy injury history that clouds the picture. He had a serious back injury late in the 2024 season, even traveling to Colombia this offseason for stem-cell therapy to treat it . He also missed time in 2025 with a knee injury and a concussion.

Another potential negative includes his contract and the cost of the trade. Jurgens' deal averages $17 million per year — a full $10 million APY lower than what Linderbaum got from the Ravens — but it's still among the highest at the position. And because of the guaranteed money left on his contract, the Ravens are probably tied to him for this season and next at the very minimum.

Giving up the 2028 second-rounder is the real eye-opener; this isn't loose change we're talking about. What the Ravens gave up was a little more than what the Cowboys traded for Joey Porter Jr. , and even if it came with cost control, it's a steeper cost for a lower-tier position.

There's a potential payoff here for the Ravens, and it's always a good sign when talented teams make aggressive moves to get better, but this is no risk-free trade.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce face new challenge in 1587 Prime trademark fight as opposing side refuses to back down
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are asking a New York federal court to drop them from the 1587 Prime trademark case, and the sneaker brand suing them is
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are asking a New York federal court to drop them from the 1587 Prime trademark case, and the sneaker brand suing them is fighting back. 1587 Sneakers sued in February over the Kansas City steakhouse's name and merchandise. The players say New York has no power over them and that they hold no direct control of the restaurant. The brand says their role goes well beyond lending a name. A judge has already refused one emergency order, but no ruling on dismissal has been reported.Why 1587 Sneakers is refusing to back down in the 1587 Prime trademark fightPatrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce moved to dismiss on three grounds: no personal jurisdiction, wrong venue, and a complaint that does not say either player personally committed an infringing act. They also deny being members of the LLC that runs the restaurant.The sneaker company's answer is blunt. Its filing says the players are recasting themselves as distant celebrities and "pretty faces" with no New York ties. The brand then points to the restaurant's own website, which says 1587 Prime was co-founded by Mahomes and Kelce in partnership with Noble 33. It also cites national advertising and promotion to argue the New York link is real.That is a sensible line of attack. Any one of the three grounds, if the judge agrees, could end the players' part in the case.Timing is the other fault line. 1587 Sneakers says it began selling on April 13, 2023, so it claims first use, yet it did not apply for the "1587" trademark until October 2025. The "1587 Prime" trademark was filed in December 2023 in the bar and restaurant category. Each side can say it came first, just in a different way.What the dispute means for Mahomes, Kelce and the steakhouseFor now, the restaurant stays open. In March, District Judge Naomi Reice Buchwald declined to sign a temporary restraining order, saying the complaint did not clearly establish personal jurisdiction or proper venue in New York. The order did not dismiss the lawsuit.The brand wants more than a new name. It is seeking an injunction against use of the 1587 mark, plus damages, attorney's fees and costs, and says consumers wrongly believe it is tied to the restaurant and the players. The suit also notes that 1587 Prime sells clothing as merchandise.That detail matters most. A steakhouse and a shoe label do not chase the same diners, but apparel is where the two brands meet.The jurisdiction fight may also decide how this ends. A legal expert quoted by Heavy said the case could be resolved without a judge ever deciding which side has the stronger trademark claim. The defendants' reply brief was due September 1.
