articles.title: Stephen A. Smith Apologizes for Lane Johnson Retirement Comments on Mental Health
articles.summary: ESPN personality Stephen A. Smith apologized Wednesday for his criticism of Lane Johnson's decision to retire this week after suggesting that the Philadelphia Eagles' tackle retired due to the team's struggles this season rather than the "personal and family priorities" and "mental health" reasons Johnson cited.
articles.body:
ESPN personality Stephen A. Smith apologized Wednesday for his criticism of Lane Johnson's decision to retire this week after suggesting that the Philadelphia Eagles' tackle retired due to the team's struggles this season rather than the "personal and family priorities" and "mental health" reasons Johnson cited .

Smith claimed that people "misconstrued me making light of mental health, I would never do that."

Johnson said in his retirement post that he "deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season," hence his decision not to retire before the season. Ultimately, however, he said that his priorities changed after a period of "reflection."

Across both the NFL and within Philadelphia , the response was one of understanding regarding his decision and gratitude for his 14 years with the Eagles.

The 36-year-old is a future Hall of Famer and one of the best right tackles in NFL history. He was a two-time champion, six-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro, and during his career the Eagles were a far more successful team with him on the field than off.

"I've said it before: First-ballot Hall of Famer," general manager Howie Roseman said of Johnson . "... Huge, big part of our success. Just someone you never took for granted every day. Practice, games—just felt totally honored that he was our right tackle for as long as he was. And the relationship, just having him around, and the relationship we had through all those years and through the things we had to go through with our team and what was going on with all of us personally, we'll miss him, and just very appreciative of him and his contributions to our success."

The Eagles have had quite the turnover at offensive line this season.

Longtime offensive-line coach and run-game coordinator Jeff Stoutland left his post before the season as the team shifted to a new running scheme under offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. Three-time Pro Bowler Landon Dickerson is on injured reserve with a knee injury, and after struggling with injuries last season, there are questions about his future. Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens on Tuesday alongside a 2027 seventh-rounder for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder after struggling with the move from center to guard this season.

Philly's offensive line, once one of the best units in the NFL, has struggled the past two seasons. Losing Johnson most certainly won't help, but he has the right to leave on his own terms, however abrupt the decision may have felt from the outside.

articles.title: Texans' DeMeco Ryans Takes Over Defensive Play-Calling Duties amid 0-4 Start
articles.summary: Houston Texans coach DeMeco Ryans announced Wednesday he is assuming play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Matt Burke.
articles.body:
Houston Texans coach DeMeco Ryans announced Wednesday he is assuming play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Matt Burke.

This comes as the Texans have dropped their first four games and allowed an average of 343.8 yards and 27.3 points.

Houston's defeats in Weeks 1 and 4 have been particularly tough to stomach given the performance of quarterback C.J. Stroud. He threw for 621 combined yards and four touchdowns against the Buffalo Bills and Dallas Cowboys, and that was all for naught.

Letting Burke be the defensive play-caller worked out great for Houston in 2025. The team allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points in the league.

But this isn't the first time Ryans acted decisively toward one his coordinators in the face of poor results.

Bobby Slowik generated a lot of head-coaching buzz during the 2024 hiring cycle for his work with the Texans offense. The following offseason, Houston fired him altogether as offensive coordinator after the unit went backwards.

As much as Ryans wants to say otherwise, many will see Wednesday's move as a reflection of Burke's work and how he's being evaluated internally. You don't diminish the role of a coach who you think is doing a good job.

And now Burke is put in a tough position because any improvement from the defense is likely to be credited to Ryans more so than him.

At the same time, Ryans can't worry about the optics if he genuinely believes this is a strategy that will benefit the team.

articles.title: NFL Will Stop Fining Players for 'Beverage' Celebrations, Announces Updated List of Illegal Acts
articles.summary: The NFL and NFL Players Association are clarifying rules for on-field celebrations after walking back fines for players who mimed chugging drinks after scoring touchdowns.
articles.body:
The NFL and NFL Players Association are clarifying rules for on-field celebrations after walking back fines for players who mimed chugging drinks after scoring touchdowns.

The league will no longer discipline players "imitating drinking a beverage" on the field, the NFL and NFLPA announced Wednesday.

Prohibited gestures include imitating smoking or drug use, as well as anything the league rules is sexual or depicting violence.

That includes gestures miming the use of guns or other weapons, the NFL and NFLPA said.

Other gestures described as unsportsmanlike conduct in the NFL rulebook include throat slashing or "nose wipe" gestures. The league stopped penalizing bow-and-arrow celebrations ahead of the 2025 season.

The news comes after the NFL rescinded fines for San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk and Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson , who were initially disciplined for miming drinking after Week 2 touchdowns.

The NFL said Wednesday players whose celebrations fall "into a gray area" will now be contacted and advised before any discipline is imposed.

NFLPA executive director JC Tretter said in a social media post the change came after an "unusual spike" in celebration fines.

A total of 20 celebration fines were issued to players over Weeks 2 and 3, and all 20 have since been appealed, Tretter said.

"When something falls into a gray area, communication and education should come before punishment," Tretter wrote. "We're glad the league will seek to educate players before immediately defaulting to a fine."

Both Juszczyk and Ferguson argued in their appeals they were pretending to drink non-alcoholic beverages.

The NFL noted when rescinding Juszczyk's fine the fullback had "stated that the fine is hypocritical with the amount of Bud Light sponsorships surrounding the NFL," per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

The NFL had issued 88 total fines as of Week 3. Fines for players punished for illegal celebrations have ranged from $8,847 to $14,926.

The rule changes regarding fines come amid an uptick in accepted penalties. The NFL has upheld 963 flags through Week 4, marking the highest total since at least 1978, per ESPN Insights .

articles.title: Drink up, boys! NFL reverses course after meeting with NFLPA to allow all drinking celebrations without fines
articles.summary: The NFL and NFL Players Association now allow drinking celebrations after rescinding fines for Kyle Juszczyk and Jake Ferguson's touchdown moves.
articles.body: It took nearly two weeks and a meeting of the minds from the NFL and NFL Players Association (NFLPA), but after all that high-priced talent hashed things out, we've come to a conclusion that will affect humanity. NFL players are allowed to celebrate big plays by simulating drinking. So, drink up, boys! NFL FINES PLAYER NICKNAMED 'JUICE' $14,926 FOR USING A DRINKING CELEBRATION, CALLING IT OFFENSIVE It no longer matters what's on a player's mind when he mimics drinking during a celebration. He might be thinking about sipping tea, as Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor apparently was after scoring a touchdown on Sunday in London. He might be thinking about drinking juice, as Kyle Juszczyk insisted he was doing when he was fined after Week 2. The player might be mimicking taking a drink from a Gatorade bottle as Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson claimed he was doing when he was fined. 49ERS FULLBACK KYLE JUSZCZYK SUCCESSFULLY APPEALS NFL BEER FINE BY INVOKING HIS 'JUICE' NICKNAME And even this: The player could even be thinking he's shotgunning a beer. It's fine now rather than headed for a fine. That's because the path is now clear on all drinking, sipping, chugging and shotgunning beverages in the NFL. Peace on Earth! In a joint statement issued by the league and the NFLPA on Wednesday, it was explained that celebrations including "imitating drinking a beverage" will not be considered a violation. "Football is the greatest game in the world," the NFL and the NFLPA said in a statement released jointly. "NFL players are admired by millions of fans, including young people competing at every level of the sport. "The passion emotion, and personality players bring to the field are a big part of what makes the game special and connects them with fans worldwide. Good sportsmanship is equally important: "To clarify the line between player expression and conduct that may result in discipline, players were reminded this week that the following are prohibited and may result in a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, a fine, or both: CARDINALS BACKUP CORNERBACK FINED BY NFL FOR WRITING 'GLORY BE 2 GOD' ON HIS EYEBLACK "Conversely, recent celebrations imitating drinking a beverage will not be considered violations or result in discipline. The league-wide guidance provides players with greater clarity on how they can celebrate while remaining within the rules. "When conduct falls into a gray area, the league will contact the player and provide direction before imposing discipline. The player will be advised that continued use of the identified celebration may result in future fines. "Individual and team celebrations are part of the game and help players connect with fans. Providing clear, consistent guidance allows players to express themselves while upholding the principles of sportsmanship that have long been a hallmark of NFL football." This is a pendulum that seemed to swing so violently against any sort of beverage celebration two weeks ago, flying all the way back in the other direction and then some. So much so that, as the memo states, the NFL is adopting a new approach to what it does when a player seemingly crosses a line during a celebration. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The league will communicate with the player first. If the NFL decides that the celebration will not be allowed, the player will be fined only if he continues the same celebration afterward. "We raised this issue and pushed for greater clarity around what will and won’t result in discipline," NFLPA executive director JC Tretter posted on X. "When something falls into a gray area, communication and education should come before punishment. We’re glad the league will seek to educate players before immediately defaulting to a fine." It is not known to what extent the backlash to the rash of fines and the league's marketing and sponsorship agreement with Bud Light played a role in it backtracking on Wednesday. The NFL did, for example, rescind the fines previously levied on Ferguson and Juszczyk. And Taylor will not be fined. They'll all drink to that. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Howie Roseman Addresses Notion Eagles Are Prioritizing Future After Cam Jurgens Trade to Ravens
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have not entered a rebuilding mode despite a disappointing 2-2 start, the retirement of superstar right tackle Lane Johnson and this week's surprising trade of offensive lineman Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have not entered a rebuilding mode despite a disappointing 2-2 start, the retirement of superstar right tackle Lane Johnson and this week's surprising trade of offensive lineman Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens.

"I think nothing has changed in terms of our goals," executive vice president and general manager Howie Roseman told reporters on Wednesday. "We're trying to win this year. I think from my perspective, just looking at what is the ultimate goal, which is to win the last game of the year and then have a run like we've had. Obviously, since Coach [Nick Sirianni] has been here we've made the playoffs five times and have been to two Super Bowls. You want to have an extended run so my job is to look at how we can have sustained success for a long period of time and you don't get many opportunities to get second-round picks in trades and get flexibility. I think just looking at our team, a lot of guys on long-term deals and being able to create some flexibility is a good situation for us financially and with the picks."

Stephen A. Apologizes After Lane Johnson Comments

The Eagles traded Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-rounder to Baltimore for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-rounder. The team now has two first-round picks and two second-round picks in 2028.

Jurgens had struggled this season after making the move to guard, and the team's offense in general has sputtered for a second straight campaign. Injuries to players like wideout DeVonta Smith, tight end Dallas Goedert, running backs Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby and guard Landon Dickerson haven't helped. But despite the circumstances, Roseman felt it was a trade he couldn't pass up.

"We weren't looking to move Cam," he told reporters . "... Had a chance to watch Drew [Kendall] here play center. He's doing a nice job, have a young player there. I think for us, when you talk about [the second-rounder] and the [fifth-rounder] and going from the seventh to the fifth, we've had success in the fifth round. Plus, the money, plus Drew playing, we felt like we were getting four players for one. We just felt like for us with all of these guys that we've got coming up, a lot on the defensive side of the ball we want to re-sign and extend, felt like that was a good situation for us."

articles.title: New NFL Rumors Reveal Browns QB Plans for Watson, Shedeur, More Amid Gabriel Injury Return
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns reportedly plan on using four of the spots on their 53-man roster on the quarterback position.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns reportedly plan on using four of the spots on their 53-man roster on the quarterback position.

Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com reported Wednesday the AFC North team prefers to keep Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel and sixth-round pick Taylen Green on the roster with Gabriel now designated to return.

The Oregon product has been on injured reserve with a back injury.

Watch Shilo Sanders Take Shedeur House Hunting in Fort Lauderdale in New Video

The battle for the starting quarterback position between Watson and Sanders was a major storyline in training camp for the Browns, but the former ended up winning it.

And the team is off to an excellent start and improved to 3-1 with its 27-24 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4. It has won three games in a row following an opening loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and scored a season-high amount of points against Pittsburgh.

Watson has completed 69.6 percent of his passes for 855 yards, six touchdowns and two interceptions while adding 127 yards as a runner.

He will surely remain in the starting role as long as the team is winning and he is healthy, but there will be plenty of depth behind him if the Browns do, in fact, keep four quarterbacks on the active roster.

Cabot noted they wouldn't be the only team to do so in the league this year, as the Atlanta Falcons, Philadelphia Eagles and Steelers have also kept four signal-callers.

That Cleveland wouldn't want to move on from its other three quarterbacks behind Watson on the depth chart also isn't surprising. After all, it just selected Sanders and Gabriel in the 2025 NFL draft and Green in the 2026 NFL draft.

They are all young signal-callers who could have bright futures ahead of them, and Watson is playing on the final year of his deal.

The Browns could be looking at a different quarterback situation entirely without their starter next season and likely want to further evaluate their three younger options by keeping them on the roster.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ $4.7M donation scandal takes a turn as viral charity story is debunked
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has built a strong reputation for supporting charitable causes, but a viral claim about the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback giving away
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has built a strong reputation for supporting charitable causes, but a viral claim about the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback giving away $4.7 million is not part of that record. A social media post claimed Mahomes donated an entire bonus and endorsement earnings to charities and homeless relief. The story spread rapidly across Facebook, Instagram and X before Snopes investigated it and rated the claim false.Patrick Mahomes $4.7 million donation claim was falseThe rumor gained traction in April 2025 through a Facebook group called Kansas City Chiefs Fans. One post claimed Mahomes had donated his entire $4.7 million bonus and endorsement earnings to charitable organisations and homeless relief efforts.The post attracted significant attention, receiving more than 100,000 reactions, 6,300 comments and 10,000 shares, according to Snopes. Other social media users repeated the claim, with some praising Mahomes for what they believed was an extraordinary act of generosity.One Facebook user wrote, "His actions speak a lot more than words. May he be blessed as well as the charities to receive his gift."However, Snopes found no credible news reports confirming that Mahomes had made such a donation. The fact-checking organisation searched several major search engines and found no reliable coverage supporting the claim.Snopes ultimately rated the $4.7 million donation story False.The lack of credible reporting was a major warning sign. A donation of that size involving one of the NFL's most recognisable players would normally generate coverage from multiple established news organisations, particularly if it involved a major homeless relief initiative.AI-generated image helped fuel Patrick Mahomes rumorThe social media post did not rely only on text. It also included an image that appeared to show Mahomes signing a large check.Snopes identified several signs that the image had been manipulated or generated using artificial intelligence. The writing on the check did not form meaningful words, while other parts of the image contained distorted details. The Kansas City Chiefs logo on Mahomes' clothing also appeared unclear.That detail is significant because convincing-looking images can make false stories feel legitimate. Once the picture was shared alongside a dramatic claim, users could easily assume the donation had been independently confirmed.Snopes also examined the Facebook group where the claim first gained major attention and found signs that some administrators and moderators may have been inauthentic accounts. Several profiles contained unusual employment or location information and limited identifying details.The rumor appeared during a period when similar false stories about athletes giving away large sums of money were circulating online. Snopes noted that another untrue claim falsely alleged golfer Rory McIlroy had donated his $4.2 million Masters winnings to charity.Mahomes does have a documented history of philanthropy, which may have made the latest claim appear believable. His charitable work has included support for children, education and community programmes. But genuine past donations do not make every new claim about his generosity true.The $4.7 million story is a reminder that viral charity claims involving celebrities should be checked against reliable sources before being shared. articles.title: Malik Nabers Gives Knee Injury Update After Missing Practice Before Giants vs. Commanders
articles.summary: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers provided an update regarding the health of his knee heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Washington Commanders.
articles.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers provided an update regarding the health of his knee heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Washington Commanders.

"Just sore," Nabers said Wednesday, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan . "Just sore.

"We'll see how the next day goes, but through the week, I'm usually sore. But this one was kind of a little bit more sore. I always continue to fight through it."

Nabers didn't participate in New York's practice on Wednesday due to knee issues.

He previously underwent a procedure to repair a torn ACL that he suffered in Week 4 of his 2025 campaign. Nabers also had surgery to clean up scar tissue around his knee that was causing stiffness in April.

He was limited in practice to open training camp as he worked his way back onto the field. Nabers was also listed as questionable heading into Week 1 due to his knee.

Still, he's been able to suit up in all four of New York's regular-season contests this year.

In his four appearances, he's hauled in 18 receptions for 208 yards and one touchdown. Nabers is coming off a six-catch, 112-yard performance against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4.

He's helped the Giants open the year with a 3-1 record despite losing quarterback Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury .

Nabers' activity in practice is something to monitor as New York prepares to face a Washington secondary that has struggled this season, ranking No. 25 among all teams by allowing 242.5 yards per game through the air.

Kickoff between the Giants and Commanders is on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Howie Long reveals what Sean McVay must do to save Rams’ season
articles.summary: Through four games of the NFL Season, the Los Angeles Rams have looked more human than they were anticipated to be. Raiders legend and Hall of Famer Howie Lo...
articles.body:
Through four games of the NFL Season, the Los Angeles Rams have looked more human than they were anticipated to be .

Raiders legend and Hall of Famer Howie Long told The Post's Adam Schein on "Schein Time" why Rams coach Sean McVay can still save the season, while acknowledging he hasn't been impressed with the team's recent play.

Los Angeles is coming off a gritty, come-from-behind 24-20 road victory against the Philadelphia Eagles , to improve to 2-2.

Long said that he was a "bit disappointed last week," and wants to see more production on third-down situations.

"They don't have a closer on third down, really a real closer — just a guy who throws the fear of God into you," Long said. "And I think that impacts them."

McVay is only 40 years old but might be one of the most experienced coaches in the NFL, as he's in the middle of his 10th season coaching in the NFL.

Last season, the Rams offense was injured at the receiver position, and Long said he enjoyed watching McVay adjust by sending three tight ends out on the field to help with the running game.

Now, the roles have been reversed as the tight ends have been banged up while the receivers have been healthy, so McVay has been once again adjusting his offense and relying on pre-snap motions with the wideouts.

While reigning MVP Matthew Stafford threw two interceptions on Sunday, he also threw for 317 yards in the pouring rain. Wide receiver Puka Nacua, who was sidelined for their previous two games due to a groin injury, returned to the field and spent a majority of it being motioned before the snap.

The result went as the Rams offense had hoped, as he had 12 targets come his way, with nine of them being hauled in, collecting 125 yards.

"I think Sean McVay is brilliant," Long said.

The segment on the Rams ended as Long spoke about the challenge that is the rest of the NFC West.

This Sunday, the Rams will be off, as they will play on Monday night in a home game against the Buffalo Bills, while their division rivals, the Seattle Seahawks and the San Francisco 49ers, will face off in an NFC Divisional Round rematch for first place in the NFC West.

Long said he knows McVay and the Rams will be glued to their seat watching that game.

"He's so invested in everything. He wants to win so badly," Long said. "He understands — he comes from a family that's been around football for a long time, so he understands what it's all about."

articles.title: Notre Dame to face Stanford head coach Tavita Pritchard for 1st time
articles.summary: Notre Dame has had the upper hand in matchups against Stanford over the years. The Irish will face Cardinal coach Tavita Pritchard for the 1st time.
articles.body:
US LBM Coaches Poll No. 3 Notre Dame is set to take on Stanford this weekend.

The undefeated Fighting Irish (5-0) will face 1st-year Cardinal head coach Tavita Pritchard, who has led Stanford to a 2-3 record so far .

Pritchard's college career as a coach and a player has been mainly with Stanford. He played for the Cardinal from 2006 to 2009, and was Stanford's starting quarterback between 2007 and 2009.

In his coaching career, Pritchard was at Stanford from 2011 to 2017 as a defensive assistant, a running backs coach, a QB/receiver coach and as the Cardinal's offensive coordinator that primarily focused on QBs.

Pritchard moved on to become the QB coach for the Washington Commanders. He guided QB Jayden Daniels to be the recipient of the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year award in 2024.

Check out pictures from Notre Dame’s win at North Carolina

After one more season with the Commanders in 2025, Pritchard returned to Stanford as the head football coach. While Pritchard has never faced Notre Dame in his coaching career, he has history against the Irish as a player.

Pritchard went 0-2 against Notre Dame in his playing career, losing 21-14 and 28-21, respectively, in 2007 and 2008. Pritchard was a combined 28-of-42 on completions for 284 yards, two touchdowns and five interceptions in those games.

The Irish are 24-14 all-time against the Cardinal. Notre Dame has won three in a row versus Stanford, including a 49-20 result in November of last season.

The Cardinal are coming off a 57-3 loss to Wake Forest last weekend, while the Irish are fresh off a 37-26 victory over North Carolina .

Notre Dame and Stanford will square off on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on NBC.

articles.title: Raiders Week 5 vs Patriots features Super Bowl LX rematch
articles.summary: The Patriots will face another Super Bowl rematch this week when the Raiders come to town.
articles.body:
The Patriots already lost their *technical* Super Bowl rematch when the Seahawks beat them 13-10 in the opener. The one big difference there was the offensive coordinator for the Seahawks when they beat the brakes off of them in the Super Bowl is no longer with the team.

That man is Klint Kubiak. He is now the head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders . And THAT rematch is set for this Sunday in New England.

Kubiak's offense in Seattle was third in the league in points scored. Through four games without him, they are 10th. while Kubiak's new team is eighth.

In the Super Bowl, the Seahawks pummeled the Patriots. Seattle was up 29-7 with under three minutes left in the game.

An interesting wrinkle here is the Patriots offensive coordinator both in the Super Bowl and now is former Raiders head coach Josh McDaniels. He is calling the plays for the 30th ranked offensive in the league in terms of points scored.

Safe to say the Raiders have the better end of things from an offensive scheming perspective in this rematch.

articles.title: Ladd McConkey Injury Update: Chargers WR Misses Practice (Foot)
articles.summary: Ladd McConkey has battled injuries throughout the 2026 season, and his foot injury could keep him out of the lineup in Week 5. Originally entering the league...
articles.body:
Ladd McConkey has battled injuries throughout the 2026 season, and his foot injury could keep him out of the lineup in Week 5. Originally entering the league as a second-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft , the Georgia product took the league by storm and immediately established himself as one of Justin Herbert's most reliable targets. Starting in 14 games while making 16 appearances, the wideout finished his inaugural campaign with 82 receptions for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns on 112 targets. While he wasn't quite as effective in Year 2, he remained a key part of the offense.

Now entering Week 5, Ladd McConkey has been one of the few consistent weapons in the Los Angeles Chargers offense, but he may not be able to help the team earn its first win of the season. While he doesn't have an official designation, the Chargers official account revealed the wide receiver did not practice on Wednesday.

Ladd McConkey Injury Update: Chargers WR Misses Practice

It's hard to overstate just how important Ladd McConkey is for the Chargers to have any shot at pulling an upset against the Denver Broncos. At 0-4, the Chargers playoff hopes are all-but over, and they desperately need to defeat their division rival if they want to keep even the slightest chance of playoff hopes alive.

It's hard to call any game a "must-win" this early in the season, but that's exactly what Week 5 is for the Los Angeles Chargers. At 0-4, the team is already four games behind the Kansas City Chiefs and their Wild Card chances are starting to slip as well. There is no precedent for an 0-5 team to make the playoffs, and Ladd McConkey is pretty much the only shot this team has of moving the football. Seattle has one of the league's best defenses, and the Chargers will need their top receiver to play his best football if they want to come out on top.

articles.title: Eagles’ Jalen Hurts Reacts to Abrupt Departures of Lane Johnson, Cam Jergens
articles.summary: This week, two of the five players responsible for blocking for Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts have left the team.First, star right tackle...
articles.body:
This week, two of the five players responsible for blocking for Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts have left the team.

First, star right tackle Lane Johnson retired from football due to personal reasons and then the Eagles traded center Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens for draft capital. Left tackle Jordan Mailata is now the last remaining starter on Philadelphia's offensive line from the dominant unit that helped lead the Eagles to a Super Bowl victory less than two years ago.

Jalen Hurts Wishes Nothing But the Best for Lane Johnson, Cam Jurgens

During his weekly media availability ahead of Philadelphia's Week 5 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars, Hurts wished the best for both Johnson and Jurgens and reflected fondly on the collective accomplishments of the group.

"You can't replace what we've done and all the things that we've accomplished together, the memories," Hurts said. "I've got a lot of love for Lane [Johnson] and Cam [Jurgens], and I have a lot of gratitude and appreciation for the time that we spent together, the games we played together, the adversities we've overcome, and so I wish them nothing but the best with my sincerest heart."

Hurts also acknowledged that it was difficult for him to process the retirement of Johnson, a guy who Hurts has played his entire career with, in the middle of the season when so much of his focus has to be dedicated to preparation and game-planning.

"It's a different thing for me to process in the middle of the season as a player," Hurts said, via The Philadelphia Inquirer . "I think as a person, I wish to see him smiling again. I wish to see him happy and at peace, and that's what I sincerely wish for him. So as a player, hard to … not hard to process, but really hard to focus on, considering the urgency that I have to win."

Jalen Hurts Expresses Excitement About Eagles' New-Look Offensive Line

Playing without two of the five guys that he's played behind for the past several seasons will be an adjustment for Hurts. But, he expressed excitement about competing with a new-look line that features young players like Drew Kendall, Willie Lampkin, and Markel Bell.

"Yeah, they're some funny guys. Funny, hungry, younger guys to say the least. So, you know, it's a lot to be excited for in that sense. You get the opportunity to go out here and play," Hurts said. "I know they're very hungry. I know they're excited for the opportunity to come, whatever that looks like. And at the end of the day, you want all hands on deck in it. So we're going to commit to that, commit to one another, and go out here and fight."

The new-look line will have a tough task right out of the gate facing off against a Jaguars defense that has recorded 10 sacks on the season.

Baltimore Ravens CB Marlon Humphrey was one of President Donald Trump's guests at his recent appearance in Baltimore.

"That was a little surprising. It was not how things were supposed to go. But President Trump asked us if we wanted to ride with him, and I wouldn't turn down a ride from the President. I didn't really think about the, I guess… You know me, but that was quite the experience to be in that very armoured vehicle."

"To be honest, I did not vote. I don't think I have ever voted. I did try to vote this last time, but my absentee ballot never came in. I don't really have any political beliefs, but I do plan on voting the next time around."

Trump was in Baltimore as part of an event to celebrate a $3.8 billion submarine shipyard at Sparrows Point, something Humphrey supports as a boost to the local economy of the city.

Johnson had been referring to Chicago's upcoming matchup with their fierce divisional rival Green Bay Packers after just masterminding his side's latest win over the New York Jets.

"F*** the Packers! F*** them! I f****** hate those guys!" said an animated Johnson in the Bears locker room. Again, he does not care, nor does he care for those Packers.

By modern standards he is something of an obscurity. In an era when half of NFL sidelines tend to include a disciple of Kyle Shanahan or Sean McVay, he comes from a different branch with his own interpretation of the motion-fuelled play-action zone-run Shanahan system.

Pre-snap motion and subterfuge remain paramount like any good Shanahan offense, but Johnson is creating a new kind of horizontal and diagnosis stress for defenses, whose coverage plans have no place to hide against him. He sees and induces moves on the chess board before they even happen.

Through four weeks Johnson's offense ranks first in yards with an average of 429 per game, as well as topping the rushing charts with an average of 196.3 yards on the ground. The Bears are meanwhile third in dropback success rate and eighth in EPA/play despite spending the last two weeks without starting quarterback Caleb Williams.

Johnson lost Williams to a hamstring injury late in Chicago's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week Two. It would be easy to look back on that game with some question marks around the Bears buzz, but this was a Brian Flores blitz-centric defense we are talking about. It happens to the best of the league from time to time.

His team has since averaged 434 yards and 25 points per game in back-to-back victories over the Philadelphia Eagles and, most recently, the Jets.

The 27-7 win over Philadelphia arrived behind 38-year-old backup quarterback Case Keenum, who finished 24 of 34 passing for 247 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions while making his first start in almost three years. A week later he orchestrated a 23-12 win over the Jets behind Tyson Bagent, who finished 25 of 34 passing for 268 yards and an interception in just his fifth career start.

History suggests the most gifted and successful coaches in football are still able to find ways to win no matter who is serving them under center. By doing so Johnson is thrusting himself firmly among the elite architects of his time. Right up there with the Shanahans and McVays. Plug-and-play mastery.

In both games without Williams the Bears head coach leaned on the league's most effective and dynamic rushing attack as a foundation for success behind his backup play-callers. D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai combined for 115 yards from 30 carries on the ground against the Eagles, followed by 204 rushing yards from 45 of Chicago's 54 total carries against the Jets. The latter saw Monangai lead the way with 146 yards and two touchdowns as the Bears dominated time of possession, holding the ball for 42.45 minutes to the Jets' 17.15.

It also marked the first time a team had recorded more first downs (34) than offensive plays by their opponent (32) since September 1999.

Success by way of Bagent was no fluke. Johnson has been banking on it, planning for it, assured of the quarterback depth seemingly mandatory to any productive team in today's NFL. Sure, Plan A is Williams. Should Plan Bagent and Plan Keenum come into play, he is more qualified than the majority of the league to survive and thrive.

"I do think there's a lot of merit to having a strong number two quarterback, which he certainly fits that bill. I'm of the mind that he's probably one of the best 32 in the NFL," Johnson said on Bagent earlier this summer.

Johnson's rise to stardom came with the Detroit Lions as he resurrected the career of quarterback Jared Goff within, at its peak, the most creative offense in football. A running back tandem of Jahmyr Gibbs and David Montgomery was the quintessential picture of Johnson's offense, mixing electric speed and flair with hard-nosed running between perfectly-crafted lanes. Coveted balance teed up play action production to Amon-Ra St Brown and Jameson Williams as a field-stretching attack capable of hurting rivals at every level, in every way, at every moment. It was offensive football at its breathtaking best, attacking every corner of the field, from all angles and at an unrelenting rate of success.

He prided and still prides himself on invention. One occasion last January saw Johnson roll out offensive lineman Theo Benedet on a seam route against the Packers. He also utilised six-foot-nine reserve offensive lineman Dan Skipper as a dwarfing receiver, unleashing him on isolated routes in one game and teeing him up for a trick play touchdown catch on another. Penei Sewell would meanwhile become a prominent decoy to a smoke-and-mirrors running game, Johnson's counter-flow system wreaking havoc in the face of lane discipline and play identification for defenses. His bag of tricks became the most in-demand of its kind in the NFL, prompting the Bears to turn to him as their man to lead Williams forward.

In fact, it was for Williams that Johnson decided to make Chicago his home once the head coaching jobs came calling.

His trickery has shown no sign of drying up. Johnson underlined his quarterback situation in Johnson style last Sunday as he deployed both Keenum and Bagent in the same formation on the opening drive of their win over the Jets. Only he could somewhat poke fun at his ability to win with backup quarterbacks over the last two weeks.

Johnson has become a refreshing necessity to modern football, asserting himself as one of the most impactful and innovative offensive minds of his generation while also retaining a notion of nostalgia to his rah-rah competitiveness. He is football through and through, the blend of guile and passion bringing an entire city behind him in the process.

Aaron Rodgers previously claimed he owned the Bears during his monopoly on the rivalry in Green Bay. Johnson has ripped up said script as he seeks to rewrite Chicago supremacy. His team claimed two of three games between the teams last season, including the playoff victory, while winning their first NFC North title since 2018. Before then

"He wants to beat them really bad like everyone else in the room, like every Chicago fan. Beat them real bad, and make them quit," said receiver Luther Burden III this week.

As for Packers head coach Matt LaFleur, he resisted the temptation to bite on any early mind games.

"This game is about players," he said. "And so we'll keep it about the players. You know, I'm not the one out there. They're playing. So, I think that's always been my mentality, and we're gonna keep it about those guys."

Packers safety Evan Williams added: "It's easy to have a camera in front of you and say whatever you want. That's not going to stop you from getting hit in the mouth on any given Sunday... It's not going to show up on Sunday. It's not going to save you."

Chicago had won one playoff game since 2006 prior to his arrival in 2025. Johnson has transformed the Bears, while becoming one of the most important figures in football. The NFL is better with his art and his antics in it.
